title: Zuppa di Lenticchie
subtitle: Italian lentil soup with rosemary and tomato
excerpt: A thick Umbrian lentil soup with the characteristic trio of rosemary, garlic, and tomato. Made with the small green lentils from Castelluccio that hold their shape, or with regular brown lentils that partially dissolve into the broth.

recipe.sourceNotes: Lentil soup is a staple across central Italy, particularly in Umbria and Tuscany. The celebrated lentils of Castelluccio di Norcia, an Umbrian plateau town, are considered the finest in Italy and are used in this soup. They are small, greenish-brown, and cook without soaking, holding their texture better than most lentils. The combination of lentils with rosemary, garlic, tomato, and good olive oil is the Umbrian house style.

content.text: Lentil soup in the Italian style is not a blended puree, the lentils should be whole or slightly broken, in a thick, deeply flavoured broth. Finish with the best olive oil you have; it will be one of the last flavours you taste, and it matters. A heel of Parmesan rind in the pot from the start adds depth without asserting itself.

Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, celery, and carrot for 10 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, rosemary, and chilli if using. Cook for 2 minutes. Add the tomato puree and stir for 1 minute.

Add the tinned tomatoes and stock. Bring to a boil and add the lentils. Simmer, partially covered, for 35 to 40 minutes until the lentils are completely soft. If the soup is too thick, add a little more water.
Remove the rosemary sprigs. Taste for salt and pepper. Ladle into bowls and finish with a generous drizzle of olive oil and black pepper. Serve with crusty bread.
